title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page (numbered '2' at the top) with handwritten blue corrections. The whole page is crossed out with diagonal strokes, so it is a discarded draft. The setting continues from the previous page, which is not shown typed here.

Setting:
- S is a base and G an S-group sheaf acting on a sheaf V (presumably a vector bundle or linear scheme).
- W is a subsheaf of V.
- N is the stabilizer (normalizer) of W in G.
- G/N is the orbit of W in the 'Grassmannian' of subobjects of V, i.e. the subsheaves W' locally G-conjugate to W.

The incidence object is X ⊂ G/N ×_S V, the set of pairs (W', v) with v ∈ W'. It comes with the map i : X → G/N ×_S V and the projections p : X → G/N and ψ : X → V.

The earlier cartesian diagram (x) pulls X back along G → G/N, giving Z = G ×_{G/N} X. Then Z(S') is the set of pairs (g, v) with v ∈ g·W_{S'}. The map (g, w) ↦ (g, g·w) identifies Z with G ×_S W, which gives the cartesian square (xx), with q(g, w) = (ḡ, g·w).
- Z → X is an N-torsor for the action (g, v)·n = (gn, v).
- Transported to G ×_S W, the action becomes (g, w)·n = (gn, n⁻¹·w).
- Hence X ≅ G ×^N W, the contracted (associated) product, i.e. the homogeneous vector bundle over G/N with fibre W.

Diagram (D) summarizes the maps. The key one is the 'collapsing' map ψ : G ×^N W → V, with φ = ψ∘q given by φ(g, w) = g·w.
- For a section v of V, the fibre X_v = ψ⁻¹(v) is the functor of conjugates W' of W containing v. It is a closed sub-'Schubert-type' locus of G/N.
- The fibre φ⁻¹(v) is isomorphic to M_v = {g ∈ G : g⁻¹·v ∈ W}. The page breaks off just before this definition.

Purpose: this is a standard geometric set-up, a resolution or correspondence of Springer/Kempf collapsing type. Its role in the dossier on algebraic cycles (the previous page mentions specialization of linear families, K-equivalence of cycles, Riemann–Roch) is presumably to study families of linear subspaces through a point, or a moving/dimension-count argument. The page itself proves nothing beyond these identifications.
errors: No mathematical errors. The N-torsor claims are correct, provided N stabilizes W and G/N exists as an fppf quotient sheaf; representability is not discussed on this page.
The definition of M_v is cut off at the bottom of the page. Presumably M_v = {g ∈ G : g⁻¹·v ∈ W}.

ideas.what: Incidence correspondence X = {(W', v) : v ∈ W'} over the orbit G/N of a subobject W, identified with the contracted product G ×^N W via the N-torsor G ×_S W → X with action (g, w)·n = (gn, n⁻¹w)
ideas.modern_name: associated (homogeneous) bundle G ×^N W; quotient by a free right action
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Serre's espaces fibrés algébriques, 1958); general torsor/contracted-product formalism by Grothendieck and Giraud
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (quotients, contracted products); Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne

ideas.what: Collapsing map ψ : G ×^N W → V, (g, w) ↦ g·w, with fibres = conjugates of W containing v, and the fibre of φ being M_v = {g : g⁻¹v ∈ W}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Springer (1969), Kempf (1976) for collapsings; classical incidence-variety arguments earlier

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, crossed-out typed draft setting up an incidence correspondence and associated bundle G ×^N W with its collapsing map to V. It is standard torsor bookkeeping with no new result, and the page is not even clearly in Grothendieck's own hand, apart from the corrections.
transcription_corrections: The whole page is struck through with diagonal lines, i.e. it is a discarded draft; there is a typed page number '2' at the top right.
Line 'fibré principal [xxxx] de base X et de groupe N': 'de base' and 'et' are handwritten insertions replacing a struck typed word.
'Nous résumons les principaux morphismes précédents dans le diagramme suivant' — the handwritten replacement for 'Nous [considérer]'.
'Si v est une section' — the handwritten 'v' overwrites a struck symbol. 'X_v' is written by hand over a typed letter.
'isomorphe au sous-faisceau M_v de G [formé] donné par' — the final bottom-left scribble is illegible handwriting, not a formula 'M_v'.
In (D), pr_1 and pr_2 are dashed arrows from G/N ×_S V to G/N and V respectively.
